newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish Jyske Bank 96 net up but below forecast.
newsitem.headline: Danish Jyske Bank 96 net up but below forecast.

text.p: Denmark's fourth biggest banking group Jyske Bank on Thursday posted improved but lower than expected 1996 pre-tax profits and forecast a better result in 1997.
"The Danish economic outlook looks promising. 1997 looks like being a good year with satisfactory earnings," Jyske Bank said in a statement published with its 1996 results.
It forecast 1997 profit before tax, extraordinary items and securities earnings of 600-750 million crowns, compared to 657 million crowns in 1996.

The bank's 1996 profit before tax and extraordinary items was 993 million crowns, against average expectations by a Reuter panel of analysts of 1.034 billion crowns, but better than 1995's 961 million crown surplus.

"The result lives fully up to our expectations. Seen against a background of stiffer competition, lower interest rates and cautious investment policy, Jyske's 1996 result must be deemed to be very satisfactory," the report said.
Jyske's costs rose five percent to 1.528 billion crowns last year from 1995's 1.460 billion. Core earnings fell to 1.003 billion crowns from the previous year's 1.068 billion crowns.
"1996 saw a lot of one-off expenses due in part to restructuring schemes, " Jyske said.
The bank's net profit fell to 645 million crowns from 1995's 725 million crowns surplus.
It increased its dividend to 10 percent from eight percent, describing the rise as "a signal that Jyske Bank is well prepared for the future both as regards earnings and capital".

The market was less enthusiastic than Jyske about its 1996 result. The Jyske result was announced before the Copenhagen bourse opened and the share fell five crowns at the start of trading, before firming two crowns to 538 by 1010 gmt.

"The result was rather disappointing. The Jyske share is down five-10 crowns from Wednesday but it will probably trade within the 535-540 crown range today, more or less holding its current level," a dealer told Reuters.
